title: Selvage Session Protocol — every event
description: The seven events a server sends, with the params of each. Valid against PROTOCOL.md §6. Event `params` are flat objects; an event name a receiver does not know is ignored, like an unknown member.

peerList.description: The peers already in the room, excluding `self`. No order is promised, so a receiver must not depend on one.

anyEventName.description: An event name. The seven below are defined by this protocol; any other, including every `x.`-prefixed name, is ignored rather than refused (contrast `unknown_method`).

roomCreated.description: `room.created`: the reply to a `session.hello` that minted a room. The minting connection is the room's host — by holding the private half of the host keypair whose public half the invite's fragment carries, not by the server saying so — and it is told the invite token here and nowhere else.

token.description: Present only here: the token is echoed exactly once, to the connection that minted the room, and a host that may have to reconnect must keep it (§9.1).

roomJoined.description: `room.joined`: the reply to a `session.hello` that joined an existing room. It never carries `token`, and it carries no listing: the room's documents are the host's sealed state, which arrives over the relay after this frame.

peerJoined.title: peer.joined
peerJoined.description: To the peers already present when a connection is seated. It has one meaning: a connection was seated. It is also the trigger for the room's host to re-announce the sealed room state, which is what makes the roster a joiner sees a live one (`PROTOCOL.md` §7.1, §13.1).

peerLeft.title: peer.left
peerLeft.description: To the remaining peers when a connection ends. It says nothing about the room's host: who holds the host key is not the server's to know. A departing peer's holds and presence expire on their own lease rather than by this event (`PROTOCOL.md` §13.7).

peerRenamed.title: peer.renamed
peerRenamed.description: To every peer, the one that renamed included, when a peer changes its own display name. It carries no `awareness_client_id`: the rename changes no awareness and the join is already known.

roomGone.title: room.gone
roomGone.description: To the peers left in a room when the room is destroyed, followed by close 4003. The room is not retryable: the same link learns `room_unknown` after it (`PROTOCOL.md` §6, §9). A room whose last connection has ended has nobody left to tell, which is why the next join, and not this event, is how a destroyed room is normally met.

reason.description: Free-form and not stable: a client may log it and must not branch on it.

sessionError.title: session.error
sessionError.description: A fault that has no request to answer — a bad handshake, a fatal condition on a seated connection. It carries no `id`; a fault that answers a request is an error **response** instead (§4.2).
